target.statement: Random Forest accuracy of 99.9% on the Telecom CDR dataset (101,174 records, 17 attributes, 8,830 fraud cases) after missing-value removal, Min-Max scaling, and SMOTE balancing

compute.basis: Only a ~100k-row tabular dataset with 17 features; RF/XGBoost + SMOTE on 8 CPU cores finishes in minutes, but no training code is released so the pipeline (split order, SMOTE placement, hyperparameters) must be re-implemented from prose.

blockers: No code released (only a dataset link); preprocessing/SMOTE/split details underspecified
Reported 99.9% accuracy with 0 false positives is implausible and likely reflects leakage (SMOTE before split) or a trivially separable dataset, so exact numbers may not be reproducible
Paper text is internally inconsistent (RF vs XGBoost rankings, confusion-matrix counts vs dataset size)
title: An Efficient Machine Learning-based Framework for Detection and Prevention of Frauds in Telecom Networks
